historical_references.reference:
'Teeb' was a historic port city located on the eastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula, believed to be the modern-day Dammam, Saudi Arabia. It was an important trading hub during the ancient civilization of Dilmun, around 3000 - 1500 BCE, known for its abundant natural resources including palm trees and abundant water from the nearby oases.
Context: Ancient Civilization of Dilmun.

The term 'Teeb' re-emerged during the Islamic period as the name of the coastal region of Bahrain, which was a significant maritime emirate from the 10th to the 13th centuries CE, renowned for its pearl diving industry and strategic location at the crossroads of significant trade routes.
Context: Islamic Period Emirate of Bahrain.
